wizard.importanceTitle: How much does each of these matter to you?
wizard.importanceHint: Drag each slider. 0 means you genuinely don't care; 10 means it's the thing you'd move for. Don't overthink it — the next step sharpens your top few.
wizard.compareTitle: Your top few, head to head
wizard.compareHint: Just your {{count}} highest-rated criteria, two at a time. This is the AHP step: comparing pairs is easier to answer honestly than setting numbers, and it catches contradictions.
wizard.compareNotEnough: Rate at least two things above zero on the previous step and they'll show up here.
wizard.answered: Answered {{done}} of {{total}} pairs. Any you skip fall back to your sliders.
wizard.consistent: Your answers hang together (consistency ratio {{cr}} — under 0.10 is good).
wizard.inconsistent: Your answers contradict each other a bit (consistency ratio {{cr}}; 0.10 or under is the usual bar). The roughest pair is {{a}} vs {{b}} — worth a second look, though we'll still use your answers.
wizard.skipCompare: Clear the comparisons and just use my sliders
wizard.dealbreakersTitle: What would rule a place out entirely?
wizard.dealbreakersHint: A dealbreaker isn't a low score — it excludes a place for everyone. Use it sparingly. If we have no data for something you've made a dealbreaker, the place is flagged "unverified" rather than thrown out.
wizard.yourLoggedDealbreakers: Dealbreakers you've already logged on the Priorities page:
wizard.reviewTitle: Here's what we'll use for you
wizard.reviewHint: Your weights add up to 100%. You can retake this any time and the shortlist updates.

results.shortlistHint: Weighted sum of everyone's priorities ({{n}} answered), scored only on criteria we have data for. Open a place to see every number and where it came from.
results.nothingScored: No place has enough data to score yet. Add research on the next tab.
results.range: worst/best case if the gaps go badly or well: {{low}}–{{high}}
results.noDataAtAll: Not scored at all, for lack of any data: {{list}}
results.excludedHint: One person's dealbreaker excludes a place for the group. Change it on the quiz's dealbreakers step if that's wrong.
results.sensitivityTitle: What would flip the top pick
results.sensitivityHint: How much one criterion's weight would have to move before a different place wins. A pick that only survives a narrow band of weights isn't a strong pick.
results.needTwo: Two scored places are needed before this means anything.
results.noFlips: No single criterion's weight can change the top pick — {{leader}} wins across the whole range. That's a robust result.
results.flip: {{criterion}}: move its weight {{direction}} from {{from}} to {{to}} and {{newLeader}} wins instead.
results.dataRisk: Careful: with the gaps filled in favourably, {{list}} could overtake {{leader}}. Research those before deciding.
results.weightsTitle: What we're weighing, and where we disagree
results.weightsHint: The group's weights are the average of everyone's. Big spreads are the conversations worth having.
results.needTwoPeople: Once a second person takes the quiz, disagreements show up here.
results.inconsistentPeople: Inconsistent pairwise answers (consistency ratio over 0.10): {{list}}. Their weights still count; they may want to redo the head-to-head step.

facts.title: Research & data
facts.hint: The quiz scores a place from researched facts first, then from the Country Profile, and otherwise not at all — it never invents a number. A source is required so we can check it later.
facts.measuredPlaceholder: e.g. 1,150 mm/year; zone 8b; last frost Apr 15
facts.sourcePlaceholder: Link, agency, report, or who told us
facts.pickTarget: Pick a country or parcel first.
facts.sourceRequired: Please say where this came from — the quiz won't score an unsourced number.
facts.counts: {{researched}} researched · {{profile}} from the country profile · {{missing}} with no data
